      "body": "Run now schedules the full cleanup suite every minute instead of every 10 minutes. This affects all cleanup jobs, not just annotation cleanup, and can increase database and filesystem load tenfold. The PR description only discusses changing annotation cleanup queries, so this looks accidental or at least undocumented. If intentional, it should be called out and possibly gated or configurable; otherwise revert to the previous 10-minute interval."

      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Normal cleanup batches are logged at Error level with full ID lists",
      "body": "CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags log successful batch fetches and deletes with r.log.Error (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579) and include the entire ids slice plus a nil err value. This will generate error-level noise for normal operation and can emit very large log entries or cause large allocations when the batch size is large. Use debug or info logging and log only counts or a truncated sample of IDs."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go",
      "line": 656,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Cleanup loop may finish early if a fetched batch is deleted before the DELETE runs",
      "body": "untilDoneOrCancelled stops when a batch reports zero affected rows. With the new fetch-then-delete approach, another process can delete all IDs returned by fetchIDs before deleteByIDs executes; deleteByIDs then returns 0 even though other rows still match the cleanup condition. The job will return and defer remaining deletions to a later cycle. Consider continuing when len(ids) > 0, with a retry cap, or otherwise distinguishing 'no rows fetched' from 'fetched rows already deleted'."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go",
      "line": 609,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "SQLite IN-list construction is quadratic and unbounded",
      "body": "deleteByIDs builds the SQLite IN clause by repeatedly formatting into a growing string. For large batches (the test uses 32767 IDs) this copies the entire string on each iteration and can be slow and memory-heavy; very large batches may also exceed SQLite SQL-length limits, and non-SQLite databases have placeholder limits that are not guarded. Use strings.Builder or strings.Join, and consider chunking deletes by a safe maximum."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go",
      "line": 120,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Test cleanup is registered after inserting test data",
      "body": "In TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp, the t.Cleanup that deletes annotation and annotation_tag rows is registered after createTestAnnotations and the initial assertions. If those assertions fail before registration, the shared test database is left dirty and subsequent subtests may fail spuriously. Register the cleanup before creating data or use a guaranteed truncation step."
    }

findings.title: Cleanup job interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: Run now schedules the full cleanup suite every minute instead of every 10 minutes. This affects all cleanup jobs, not just annotation cleanup, and can increase database and filesystem load tenfold. The PR description only discusses changing annotation cleanup queries, so this looks accidental or at least undocumented. If intentional, it should be called out and possibly gated or configurable; otherwise revert to the previous 10-minute interval.

findings.title: Normal cleanup batches are logged at Error level with full ID lists
findings.body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags log successful batch fetches and deletes with r.log.Error (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579) and include the entire ids slice plus a nil err value. This will generate error-level noise for normal operation and can emit very large log entries or cause large allocations when the batch size is large. Use debug or info logging and log only counts or a truncated sample of IDs.

findings.title: Cleanup loop may finish early if a fetched batch is deleted before the DELETE runs
findings.body: untilDoneOrCancelled stops when a batch reports zero affected rows. With the new fetch-then-delete approach, another process can delete all IDs returned by fetchIDs before deleteByIDs executes; deleteByIDs then returns 0 even though other rows still match the cleanup condition. The job will return and defer remaining deletions to a later cycle. Consider continuing when len(ids) > 0, with a retry cap, or otherwise distinguishing 'no rows fetched' from 'fetched rows already deleted'.

findings.title: SQLite IN-list construction is quadratic and unbounded
findings.body: deleteByIDs builds the SQLite IN clause by repeatedly formatting into a growing string. For large batches (the test uses 32767 IDs) this copies the entire string on each iteration and can be slow and memory-heavy; very large batches may also exceed SQLite SQL-length limits, and non-SQLite databases have placeholder limits that are not guarded. Use strings.Builder or strings.Join, and consider chunking deletes by a safe maximum.

findings.title: Test cleanup is registered after inserting test data
findings.body: In TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp, the t.Cleanup that deletes annotation and annotation_tag rows is registered after createTestAnnotations and the initial assertions. If those assertions fail before registration, the shared test database is left dirty and subsequent subtests may fail spuriously. Register the cleanup before creating data or use a guaranteed truncation step.
